# Folding

Reducing a slice to one value, and mapping one slice onto another.

<h2 id="fold"><code>Fold&lt;T, A&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Fold<T, A>(items: T[..], initial: A, combine: func(A, T) -> A) -> A
```

Folds every element of `items` into an accumulator, left to right.
`items` is borrowed and read; `initial` is read by value and returned when the sequence is empty; `combine` is
called once per element with the accumulator so far and the element. The accumulator's type is independent of the
element's.
Left to right is part of the contract rather than an implementation detail: a `combine` that is not associative
gives a different answer in the other direction, and callers depend on the order.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing beyond whatever `combine` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Fold.rux#L29)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description                  |
| ---- | ---------------------------- |
| `T`  | the element type             |
| `A`  | the accumulated value's type |

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type              | Description                                   |
| --------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `items`   | `T[..]`           | the sequence to work on                       |
| `initial` | `A`               | the value to start from                       |
| `combine` | `func(A, T) -> A` | how to fold an element into the running value |

**Returns**: the value left after folding every element into it

<h2 id="fold-right"><code>FoldRight&lt;T, A&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func FoldRight<T, A>(items: T[..], initial: A, combine: func(A, T) -> A) -> A
```

Folds every element of `items` into an accumulator, right to left.
`items` is borrowed and read; `initial` is read by value and returned when the sequence is empty; `combine` is
called once per element with the accumulator so far and the element, starting from the last.
The mirror of [`Fold`](/docs/api/algorithms/folding#fold), and a different answer for any `combine` that is not associative.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing beyond whatever `combine` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Fold.rux#L51)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description                  |
| ---- | ---------------------------- |
| `T`  | the element type             |
| `A`  | the accumulated value's type |

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type              | Description                                   |
| --------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `items`   | `T[..]`           | the sequence to work on                       |
| `initial` | `A`               | the value to start from                       |
| `combine` | `func(A, T) -> A` | how to fold an element into the running value |

**Returns**: the value left after folding every element into it, from the end

<h2 id="sum"><code>Sum&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Sum<T>(items: T[..], initial: T) -> T
```

The sum of `initial` and every element of `items`.
`items` is borrowed and read; `initial` is read by value and is what an empty sequence gives back. The starting
value is asked for rather than assumed, because a generic element type has no zero this package could name.
Requires `+` on the element type. Overflow behaves exactly as `+` does on that type: this does not check, and a
caller who needs checking folds a checked addition instead.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Fold.rux#L72)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type    | Description             |
| --------- | ------- | ----------------------- |
| `items`   | `T[..]` | the sequence to work on |
| `initial` | `T`     | the value to start from |

**Returns**: `initial` plus every element

<h2 id="product"><code>Product&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Product<T>(items: T[..], initial: T) -> T
```

The product of `initial` and every element of `items`.
`items` is borrowed and read; `initial` is read by value and is what an empty sequence gives back — which is why
it must be one rather than zero for the answer to mean anything.
Requires `*` on the element type. Overflow behaves exactly as `*` does on that type.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Fold.rux#L92)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type    | Description             |
| --------- | ------- | ----------------------- |
| `items`   | `T[..]` | the sequence to work on |
| `initial` | `T`     | the value to start from |

**Returns**: `initial` times every element

<h2 id="transform"><code>Transform&lt;T, U&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Transform<T, U>(destination: var U[..], source: T[..], transform: func(T) -> U) -> bool
```

Writes `transform` of each element of `source` into `destination`.
`source` is borrowed and read; `destination` is borrowed mutably and written; `transform` is called once per
element. The two sequences may have different element types, and may be the same storage when they do not.
Reports false, having written nothing, when the two lengths differ — for the same reason [`CopyTo`](/docs/api/algorithms/modifying#copy-to) does: a
partial result is worse than a refused one when the caller cannot tell how far it got.
Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing beyond whatever `transform` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Fold.rux#L115)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description                  |
| ---- | ---------------------------- |
| `T`  | the element type             |
| `U`  | the destination element type |

**Parameters**

| Name          | Type           | Description                                         |
| ------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `destination` | `var U[..]`    | where the results go                                |
| `source`      | `T[..]`        | where the elements come from                        |
| `transform`   | `func(T) -> U` | how to turn a source element into a destination one |

**Returns**: whether `destination` was long enough to hold every result
